mainTopic: Liability for relations with a בהמה, הערה with a בהמה, and when the animal itself is killed
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא: a man or a woman with a בהמה is חייב whether כדרכה or שלא כדרכה. רב נחמן בר רב חסדא splits the cases, and רב פפא argues the split should be reversed. The ברייתא shows the הלכה follows neither of them. רבא then teaches, from an extra word in the aunts' פסוק, that הערה alone counts with a בהמה, and the גמרא explains why that hint can sit among the כרת sins. רב אשי ties a strange question about הערה on oneself to the מחלוקת about משמש מת. Students ask רב ששת whether a בהמה a גוי sinned with is killed, and he brings a קל וחומר from trees used for עבודה זרה. That leads to a debate on why a worshipped animal is not killed: אביי says the shame is small, and רבא says the animal got no pleasure. Both agree the Torah has pity on living creatures. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a proof from the משנה, which finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: both ways make one liable with an animal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that began earlier finishes. A man with a בהמה, or a woman with a בהמה, is חייב whether it is כדרכה or שלא כדרכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who has relations with an animal, whether in the normal way or not in the normal way, and a woman who brings an animal onto herself, whether in the normal way or not in the normal way, is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of a ברייתא that started before this section. It lists the cases of relations with a בהמה that make a person חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes no difference between the two ways, כדרכה and שלא כדרכה. It says this for a man with a בהמה and for a woman with a בהמה. This line is the base text that the next steps will argue about.

phrases.english: One who has relations with an animal,
whether in the normal way or not in the normal way,
and a woman who brings an animal onto herself,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כְּדַרְכָּהּ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא כְּדַרְכָּהּ – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: whether in the normal way or not in the normal way – is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַבָּא עַל הַבְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ברייתא that was quoted before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relations with a בהמה, by a man or by a woman, make a person חייב both כדרכה and שלא כדרכה.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא: two ways for a woman, one way for an animal
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא teaches that a woman with a בהמה is חייב in two ways, but a man with a בהמה is חייב in only one way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא taught: with a woman there are two kinds of lying, and with an animal there is one kind of lying.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא gives a teaching that splits the cases. A woman who is with a בהמה is חייב in both ways, but a man who is with a בהמה is חייב in only one way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treated all the cases the same. רב נחמן בר רב חסדא adds a difference: a woman has two kinds of משכב, while a בהמה has only one. So a man with a בהמה would be חייב only כדרכה.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind or way of lying, meaning a way of relations

phrases.aramaic: דָּרַשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda taught:
With a woman there are two kinds of lying,
phrases.notes: He means a woman with a בהמה is חייב in both ways.

phrases.english: and with an animal there is one kind of lying.
phrases.notes: He means a man with a בהמה is חייב only in the normal way.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an אמורא's teaching that makes a difference the ברייתא did not make.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman with a בהמה is חייב in two ways; a man with a בהמה is חייב in only one way.

steps.title: רב פפא: the logic should be the other way around
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא argues that a woman should be חייב only in her normal way. A בהמה, which has no normal way with a man at all, should make him חייב in every way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objected: On the contrary! A woman, for whom it is her normal way, is liable for that kind of lying, and not liable for anything else. An animal, for whom it is not a normal way at all, he should be liable for it in each and every opening.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges רב נחמן בר רב חסדא. He says the reasoning should be flipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא argues that a woman has a natural way of relations, so liability should be limited to that way. A בהמה has no natural way of relations with a person at all, so every way is the same, and he should be חייב in every way. So רב פפא reverses the split: one way for a woman, both ways for a בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenged it, raised a strong objection
On the contrary, it is just the opposite

phrases.english: Rav Pappa objected to it:
On the contrary! A woman, for whom it is her normal way,
is liable for that kind of lying,
and is not liable for anything else.
An animal, for whom it is not a normal way at all,

phrases.aramaic: לִחַיַּיב עֲלַהּ עַל כׇּל נֶקֶב וָנֶקֶב.
phrases.english: he should be liable for it in each and every opening.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא אַדְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of step 2 and offers the opposite split.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא's split: two ways for a woman, one way for a בהמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A natural way of relations limits liability to that way. Where there is no natural way, as with a בהמה, all ways should be equal, so the split should be reversed.

steps.title: The ברייתא goes against both opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא again to show it follows neither opinion: both a man and a woman with a בהמה are חייב in both ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in a ברייתא (not like either of them): A male nine years and one day old, one who has relations with an animal, whether in the normal way or not in the normal way, and a woman who brings an animal onto herself, whether in the normal way or not in the normal way, is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא again, this time as proof against both רב נחמן בר רב חסדא and רב פפא. The ברייתא says both cases are חייב in both ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא limited the man with a בהמה to one way. רב פפא limited the woman to one way. The ברייתא says בין כדרכה בין שלא כדרכה for both, so neither split stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Nine years and one day old

steps.whatToRemember: The final word here is the ברייתא: both a man with a בהמה and a woman with a בהמה are חייב in both ways. No split is made, not רב נחמן בר רב חסדא's and not רב פפא's.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new ברייתא. It is the same ברייתא from step 1, quoted again on purpose, now to disprove both אמוראים.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita (not like either of them):
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some leave them out. Either way, the ברייתא disagrees with both.

phrases.aramaic: זָכָר בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: A male nine years and one day old,
one who has relations with an animal,
whether in the normal way or not in the normal way,
and a woman who brings an animal onto herself,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כְּדַרְכָּהּ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא כְּדַרְכָּהּ – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: whether in the normal way or not in the normal way – is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא דְּלָא כְּתַרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא of step 1 to reject both step 2 and step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects both opinions: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא's and רב פפא's.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both opinions limit one of the cases to a single way, but the ברייתא says both cases are חייב בין כדרכה בין שלא כדרכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A man or a woman with a בהמה is חייב in both ways.

steps.title: רבינא asks about the first stage of intercourse with a male
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רבא whether a man who does only the first stage of intercourse (הערה) with another male is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רבא: One who does only the first stage of intercourse with a male, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. רבינא wants to know if הערה, a partial act, counts as a full forbidden act when done with a male.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the sugya discussed which ways of relations with a בהמה make someone חייב. Now the question is how much of the act is needed. Is the first stage alone enough for a חיוב?

keyTerms.meaning: one who does הערה, only the first stage of intercourse

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rava:
One who does the first stage of intercourse with a male, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרָבָא: הַמְעָרֶה בִּזְכוּר, מַהוּ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about partial intercourse, after the discussion of כדרכה and שלא כדרכה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does הערה alone with a male make a person חייב?

steps.title: The question about a male is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes aside the question about a male: the פסוק says 'משכבי אשה', so whatever counts with a woman counts with a male too.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who does the first stage with a male? 'As one lies with a woman' is written about him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the question about a male cannot be the real question, because the answer is already in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'משכבי אשה' compare relations with a male to relations with a woman. With a woman, הערה already counts as a full act, so the same is true with a male. That leaves nothing to ask here.

keyTerms.meaning: 'as one lies with a woman', the words of the פסוק about a male

phrases.english: One who does the first stage with a male?
'As one lies with a woman' is written about him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמְעָרֶה בִּזְכוּר – מִשְׁכְּבֵי אִשָּׁה כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the wording of רבינא's question as too obvious to ask.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The question as asked about a male only.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק already compares a male to a woman, so the answer is known.

steps.title: The real question: the first stage with an animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords רבינא's question: he must have asked about הערה with a בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, one who does the first stage of intercourse with an animal, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: Having set aside the male case, the גמרא gives the real question: does הערה with a בהמה make a person חייב? This sets up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a בהמה there is no 'משכבי אשה' comparison in the פסוק. So it really is unclear whether a partial act counts.

keyTerms.meaning: rather; it introduces a corrected version

phrases.english: Rather, one who does the first stage of intercourse with an animal, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, הַמְעָרֶה בִּבְהֵמָה, מַהוּ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected question with the true question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does הערה alone with a בהמה make a person חייב?

steps.title: רבא moves the extra word about the aunts over to an animal
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the first stage counts with a בהמה. The word about הערה written by the aunts is not needed there, so it teaches about a בהמה instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If it is not needed for the first stage written about one's father's sister and mother's sister, since it is not needed there because it was already compared to the first stage of a נדה, apply it to the first stage with an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers yes: הערה with a בהמה counts. He proves it with an 'אם אינו ענין' teaching, which takes an extra word from one place and uses it somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the aunts uses the word הערה. But that word is not needed there, because all עריות are already compared to נדה, where הערה is written. Since the word is extra, it gets moved to teach about a בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'if it is not needed for its own topic', a way of moving an extra word to teach something else
one's father's sister and mother's sister (aunts)
was compared by the Torah (a היקש)
a woman during her monthly period
give it over to teach a different topic

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not mean the word teaches nothing about the aunts. The law is the same there anyway because of the comparison to נדה. The word itself is extra, so it can teach about a בהמה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
If it is not needed for the matter of the first stage
that is written regarding
one's father's sister and mother's sister,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:19, where it says 'הערה', 'he has made bare'.

phrases.english: since it is not needed there,
because it was already compared to the first stage of a נדה,
phrases.notes: The first stage is written about נדה in ויקרא 20:18, and all the forbidden relations are compared to her.

phrases.english: apply it to the matter of the first stage with an animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לְהַעֲרָאָה דִּכְתִיבָא גַּבֵּי אֲחוֹת אָבִיו וַאֲחוֹת אִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 with a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הערה with a בהמה counts as a full act, learned through אם אינו ענין from the extra word by the aunts.

steps.title: Why hint at an animal law in a כרת section?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: בהמה is punished with מיתת בית דין, so the Torah should have written its hint among the מיתת בית דין sins, not among the כרת sins like the aunts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, an animal is among those liable to court-imposed death. Why do I need its first stage to be written among those liable to כרת? Let the Torah write it among those liable to court-imposed death, and learn court-death cases from court-death cases!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's source. A מיתת בית דין law should come from a מיתת בית דין section, not from the aunts, who only get כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The aunts are a כרת sin, while בהמה is a מיתת בית דין sin. It seems odd for the Torah to place a hint about בהמה in a section about a lighter kind of sin. If the Torah wanted to teach it, it would have put the extra word where similar cases are found.

keyTerms.meaning: 'now, since...', it opens a logical challenge
those who get a death penalty from the court
those who get כרת, a punishment from Heaven
and let one learn (one case from another)

phrases.english: Now, an animal
is among those liable to court-imposed death,
why do I need its first stage to be written
among those liable to karet?
phrases.notes: He means the aunts, who are punished with כרת and not by the court.

phrases.aramaic: לִכְתְּבֵיהּ גַּבֵּי חַיָּיבֵי מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין,
phrases.english: Let it be written among those liable to court-imposed death,
and let one learn those liable to court-imposed death
from those liable to court-imposed death!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי, בְּהֵמָה מֵחַיָּיבֵי מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source רבא used in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's derivation of הערה with a בהמה from the extra word by the aunts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A law about a מיתת בית דין sin would more naturally be hinted at in a מיתת בית דין section, so the placement by the aunts (כרת) seems wrong.

steps.title: The whole verse is extra, so it can teach about a בהמה
steps.stepSummary: The verse about the aunts is entirely extra and exists to be expounded, so the hint about הערה placed in it can teach about בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the whole verse is only there to teach something new, it can also hold a hint that teaches something else, even something outside its own topic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 9. It explains why the hint about בהמה could be written among the aunts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that a hint about בהמה belongs among the מיתת בית דין sins, not among the כרת sins. The answer is that the aunts' verse is completely extra, because the aunts are already forbidden elsewhere. A verse that exists only to be expounded can carry a lesson about any topic, so its placement does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching drawn out of the verse

steps.whatToRemember: An entirely extra verse can teach a lesson even about a topic outside its own section. That is how the aunts' verse teaches that הערה counts with a בהמה.

phrases.english: Since the entire verse
phrases.notes: This is the aunts' verse in ויקרא 20:19. The aunts are already forbidden back in ויקרא 18:12–13, so this verse is extra.

phrases.english: comes for the sake of a teaching,
a matter meant for a teaching is also written in it.
phrases.notes: He means the hint about הערה, which teaches about a בהמה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וְכוּלֵּיהּ קְרָא לִדְרָשָׁא הוּא דְּאָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 and defends רבא's answer in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the verse's location does not matter: an entirely extra verse is free to teach about any topic.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A hint about בהמה should appear among the מיתת בית דין sins, where בהמה belongs.
steps.terutzMaskana: The aunts' verse is fully extra, so it can carry the lesson about בהמה even though it sits among the כרת sins.

steps.title: A question about a man who does הערה on himself
steps.stepSummary: רב אחדבוי בר אמי asks רב ששת what the law is for a man who does the first stage of male intercourse on himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחדבוי בר אמי asked רב ששת: if a man does the first stage of the act on himself, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רב אחדבוי בר אמי asks whether a man is חייב for the sin of משכב זכר if he does הערה on his own body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since הערה already counts as the act, the question is whether doing it to one's own body counts as a forbidden act with a male. This opens a new topic, separate from the בהמה discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: One who does the first stage of intercourse (הערה)

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַחָדְבוּי בַּר אַמֵּי מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rav Achadevoi bar Ami asked Rav Sheshet:
One who does the first stage of intercourse on himself, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַחָדְבוּי בַּר אַמֵּי מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question after the בהמה discussion closes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a man who does הערה on his own body is חייב for משכב זכר.

steps.title: רב ששת brushes off the question
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers, 'You disgust me!', treating the question as unpleasant and not realistic.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You disgust me!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת refuses to deal with the question. He calls it disgusting, as if such a case could not really happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a legal ruling. רב ששת pushes the question aside, and the next step (רב אשי) shows the case is possible and explains how the law would work.

phrases.english: He said to him: You disgust me!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: קְבַסְתַּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the question of step 11 by dismissing it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case seems repulsive and practically impossible.

steps.title: רב אשי: it depends on the מחלוקת about משמש מת
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains the case is only possible without full arousal (משמש מת), so the answer depends on the known מחלוקת about that. If it is פטור there, it is פטור here. If it is חייב, he is חייב twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: What is your question? With full arousal, this cannot happen. It can only happen without full arousal. The one who says that such an act with a forbidden relative is פטור would say he is פטור here too. The one who says it is חייב would say he is חייב twice here: once as the one doing the act, and once as the one the act is done to.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question from step 11. He shows that the answer already follows from an existing מחלוקת, so there is nothing new to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי first narrows the case: it can only happen without full arousal. The law of intercourse without full arousal is already disputed. So whoever says פטור there says פטור here, and whoever says חייב there says he gets two חיובים here, because the same man plays both roles in the forbidden act.

keyTerms.meaning: What is your question? (meaning: the answer is already clear)
The one who does the act
The one the act is done to

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי: the case depends on משמש מת. If you hold פטור, he is פטור here too. If you hold חייב, he is חייב twice, as שוכב and as נשכב.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common גמרא move: a question that seems new is answered by tying it to an existing מחלוקת.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מַאי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ?
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: What is your question?
With full arousal you cannot find such a case;
you can only find it when one has relations without full arousal.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מְשַׁמֵּשׁ מֵת בַּעֲרָיוֹת פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: According to the one who says that relations without full arousal with forbidden relatives are exempt,
here too he is exempt.
And according to the one who says he is liable,
here he is liable for two:
he is liable as the one who does the act, and he is liable as the one the act is done to.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מַאי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 after רב ששת's dismissal in step 12, showing the case is possible.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case only happens without full arousal, so it follows the מחלוקת about משמש מת: either פטור, or חייב twice (as שוכב and as נשכב).

steps.title: Is the animal killed when a גוי sins with it?
steps.stepSummary: Students ask רב ששת about a גוי who sins with a בהמה. Is the animal killed only when there is both תקלה and קלון, or is תקלה alone enough?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב ששת: a גוי who sins with an animal, what is the law? Do we need both a disaster and a shame to kill the animal? Here there is a disaster but no shame. Or perhaps a disaster alone is enough, even without shame?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is asked. It sets up two possible sides about whether the animal is killed in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two reasons for killing the animal: it caused a person's downfall (תקלה), and it is a reminder of shame (קלון). With a גוי, the תקלה exists, but there is no קלון for בית דין to protect. The question is whether both reasons are needed, or whether תקלה alone is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A disaster; the animal caused a person to sin and be punished
Shame; the animal is a reminder of the shameful act

steps.confusionAlert: The question is about the animal being killed, not about punishing the גוי.

phrases.english: They asked Rav Sheshet:
A non-Jew who has relations with an animal, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He is asking whether the animal is killed, as it would be if a Jew sinned with it.

phrases.english: Do we need both a disaster and a shame,
and here there is a disaster, but there is no shame?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא תַּקָּלָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין קָלוֹן?
phrases.english: Or perhaps a disaster is enough, even though there is no shame?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת: גּוֹי הַבָּא עַל הַבְּהֵמָה מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question, unrelated to רב אשי's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether killing the animal requires both תקלה and קלון, or whether תקלה alone is enough, as in the case of a גוי where there is no קלון.

steps.title: רב ששת's proof from trees used for idol worship
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת brings a ברייתא with a קל וחומר. Trees that caused people to sin must be destroyed, so an animal that led a person into a death-penalty sin surely must be destroyed. Causing sin (תקלה) alone is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: You already learned this. Trees do not eat, drink, or smell. Yet the Torah said to destroy, burn, and finish them off, because people came to sin through them. So something that leads a person away from the ways of life toward the ways of death should be destroyed all the more.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the students' question from Step 14 by pointing to a ברייתא they already know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Trees used for עבודה זרה feel nothing and carry no great shame, yet the Torah destroys them only because they caused sin. The animal in a case of רביעה caused a much worse result: it led a person toward death. So תקלה alone is enough, and a גוי's animal is killed even though a גוי's shame is not the issue.

keyTerms.meaning: You (already) learned it, meaning a ברייתא already teaches this
Trees (here, trees used for idol worship)
A stumbling block, something that caused a person to sin
How much more so (the conclusion of a קל וחומר)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that causing sin is a reason to destroy the object. The rest of the sugya tests that rule.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: You have learned it.
If trees, which do not eat,
and do not drink and do not smell,
the Torah said: Destroy, burn, and finish off,
phrases.notes: These are trees that were worshipped as idols. See דברים 7:5 and 12:3.

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וּבָאת לְאָדָם תַּקָּלָה עַל יָדָן.
phrases.english: since a stumbling came to people through them.
One who leads his fellow astray
from the ways of life to the ways of death,
phrases.notes: He means the animal, which led the person into a sin that carries the death penalty.

phrases.english: how much more so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב ששת: תניתוה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' question in Step 14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is תקלה alone enough to kill the animal of a גוי?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. By a קל וחומר from trees, causing sin alone is enough reason to destroy the animal.

steps.title: Challenge: an animal a gentile bowed to should also be killed
steps.stepSummary: If causing sin is enough, then a גוי who bows down to his animal should make it forbidden and require it to be killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, when a גוי bows down to his animal, it should become forbidden and be killed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes רב ששת's rule further and finds a case where it seems to give the wrong result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Worshipping an animal also makes it a cause of sin, just like the trees. If תקלה alone is enough, the worshipped animal should be forbidden and killed. But we do not find such a law.

keyTerms.meaning: But now, if so (introduces a challenge from the logic just stated)
It should become forbidden (no benefit allowed)

phrases.english: But now, if so,
a gentile who bows down to his animal,
it should be forbidden and be killed?

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא מעתה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule of Step 15 by extending it
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's rule that תקלה alone requires destruction
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A worshipped animal is also a תקלה, so by this logic it should be forbidden and killed.

steps.title: A gentile cannot be stricter than a Jew
steps.stepSummary: A Jew who bows to his animal does not make it forbidden. Nothing is forbidden for a גוי that is allowed for a Jew, so the גוי's animal is not forbidden either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there anything that a Jew does not make forbidden, but a גוי does?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a question that expects the answer "no".
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know that a Jew who worships a living animal does not make it forbidden. A גוי's actions cannot create a stricter result than a Jew's. So the worshipped animal is not forbidden, even for a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there anything? (a question expecting the answer "no")
Forbidden in the case of a gentile

steps.confusionAlert: This is a question in form, but it works as an answer: there is no such thing.

phrases.english: Is there anything
that for a Jew is not forbidden
but for a gentile is forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: מי איכא מידי דלישראל לא אסר ולגוי אסר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to the law for a Jew
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גוי's worshipped animal should be forbidden because it caused sin
steps.terutzMaskana: Since a Jew's worship does not forbid the animal, a גוי's worship cannot either

steps.title: Challenge: an animal a Jew bowed to should be forbidden like in bestiality
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a Jew's worshipped animal is not forbidden, just as an animal used in רביעה is forbidden and killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the animal a Jew himself bowed to be forbidden, just as it is in a case of רביעה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges the starting point of the last answer: the law for a Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal used for רביעה is killed because it caused sin. Worship is also a sin that carries the death penalty. So why does a Jew's worship not forbid the animal in the same way?

keyTerms.meaning: Just as it is with (introduces a comparison)

phrases.english: A Jew himself, let the animal be forbidden,
just as it is with bestiality?

steps.triggerLanguage: ישראל גופיה ליתסר, מידי דהוה ארביעה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the basis of the answer in Step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that a Jew who worships his animal does not make it forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In רביעה the animal is forbidden and killed, so worship should be treated the same way.

steps.title: אביי: the shame in bestiality is much greater
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains the difference. In רביעה the person's shame is great. In animal worship it is small, so the animal is not killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: In this case (רביעה) his shame is great, and in that case (worship) his shame is small.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by pointing out a difference in קלון (shame) between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an animal used for רביעה stays alive, it is a lasting embarrassment to the person. An animal that was bowed to does not shame him nearly as much. Because of that difference, the animal is killed only in the case of רביעה.

phrases.english: Abaye said: This one, his shame is great,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the case of bestiality; "that one" in the next line is bowing down to the animal.

phrases.english: and that one, his shame is small.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר אביי: זה קלונו מרובה, וזה קלונו מועט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Worship and רביעה should be treated the same
steps.terutzMaskana: רביעה brings great shame and worship brings little shame, so only in רביעה is the animal killed

steps.title: Challenge: trees carry little shame but are still destroyed
steps.stepSummary: Trees used for idol worship do not bring great shame, yet the Torah commands that they be destroyed. So shame cannot be the deciding factor.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at trees! Their shame is not great, and still the Torah said: destroy, burn, and finish off!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's difference using the very trees from רב ששת's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If destruction depended on great shame, trees of עבודה זרה would not be destroyed. Yet the Torah does command it. This suggests that תקלה alone is enough even without great shame.

phrases.english: But look at trees, whose shame is not great,
and the Torah said: Destroy, burn, and finish off!

steps.triggerLanguage: והרי אילנות, דאין קלונן מרובה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's distinction in Step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that destruction depends on great shame
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Trees carry little shame yet are destroyed, so shame cannot be what decides.

steps.title: Living creatures are different because the Torah has pity on them
steps.stepSummary: The shame rule applies only to living animals. The Torah has pity on them, so an animal is killed only when the shame is great. Trees have no such protection.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are speaking about living creatures, because the Torah has pity on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אביי's shame rule was said only about animals, not about trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tree can be destroyed just because it caused sin. A living animal is different, because the Torah has pity on living creatures. So an animal is killed only when there is also great shame, as in רביעה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One (the Torah, or ה׳)

steps.whatToRemember: Trees used for idol worship are destroyed just for causing sin. Living animals are killed only when there is also great shame, as in רביעה, because the Torah has pity on them. That is why an animal that was worshipped is not killed.

phrases.english: We are speaking about living creatures,
for the Merciful One has pity on them.

steps.triggerLanguage: בבעלי חיים קאמרינן, דחס רחמנא עלייהו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule to its proper scope
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since trees are destroyed without great shame, animals should be too
steps.terutzMaskana: The shame requirement applies only to living creatures, because the Torah has pity on them

steps.title: רבא's reason: the animal enjoyed the sin
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that an animal used in רביעה is killed because it enjoyed the sin. A worshipped animal enjoyed nothing, so it is not killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: The Torah said that an animal that enjoyed the sin must be killed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer to the question from step 18. He offers a different reason than אביי's 'shame' reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the difference is how great the shame is. רבא says the difference is the animal itself: in רביעה the animal got pleasure from the sin, but an animal that is bowed to gets no pleasure. So only the animal in רביעה is killed.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing with step 21. He is giving a completely different answer to the question from step 18, in place of אביי's shame reason.

phrases.english: Rava says:
The Torah said,
an animal that enjoyed the sin must be killed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה, בְּהֵמָה נֶהֱנֵית מֵעֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative answer to the קשיא of step 18, replacing אביי's shame reason (steps 19-21).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A worshipped animal should be killed just like an animal used in רביעה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an animal that enjoyed the sin is killed; a worshipped animal enjoyed nothing.

steps.title: But trees enjoy nothing and are still destroyed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: trees used for idol worship get no pleasure, yet the Torah commands destroying them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at trees, which do not enjoy the sin, and still the Torah said: destroy, burn, and demolish!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's reason with the same example it used against אביי: trees used for idol worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If pleasure from the sin were the reason something is destroyed, then trees should be left alone, since trees feel nothing. But the Torah commands destroying them. So pleasure cannot be the real rule.

keyTerms.meaning: but look at, but there is the case of

phrases.english: But there are trees,
phrases.notes: These are the trees used for idol worship, the same example from step 20.

phrases.english: which do not enjoy the sin,
and the Torah said: destroy, burn, and demolish!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי אִילָנוֹת, דְּאֵין נֶהֱנִין מֵעֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reason from step 22 with the trees example.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that only something that enjoyed the sin is destroyed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Trees enjoy nothing, yet the Torah orders them destroyed, so pleasure cannot be the deciding factor.

steps.title: The rule is only for living creatures
steps.stepSummary: The rule about pleasure applies only to living creatures, because the Torah has pity on them. Trees have no such protection.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are speaking about living creatures, because the Merciful One has pity on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא with the same answer it gave for אביי in step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the Torah has pity on living creatures, an animal is killed only when there is a strong reason, here, that it enjoyed the sin. Trees are not living creatures in this sense, so they can be destroyed even without that reason.

keyTerms.meaning: the Merciful One, meaning ה׳ / the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: Both אביי and רבא agree that the Torah protects animals more than trees. They only argue about what makes an animal deserve to be killed: great shame (אביי) or the animal's pleasure (רבא).

phrases.english: We are speaking about living creatures,
since the Merciful One has pity on them.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּבַעֲלֵי חַיִּים קָאָמְרִינַן, דְּחָס רַחֲמָנָא עֲלַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 23, repeating the answer from step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule's scope (only living creatures)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pleasure rule should apply to everything, including trees.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pleasure rule protects only animals, which the Torah pities; trees are destroyed regardless.

steps.title: A proof attempt from the shame of the marketplace
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה's second reason for killing the animal: so people won't point at it and remember the person stoned because of it. It starts to draw a conclusion from this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Another reason: so that the animal will not walk through the marketplace and people will say, 'This is the one because of which so-and-so was stoned.' Is it not...?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof from the משנה to answer the earlier question about an animal used in רביעה by a גוי. The conclusion of the proof comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's second reason is about shame: the living animal reminds people of the person who was stoned. The גמרא's opening words 'is it not' show it is about to use this reason to decide whether a גוי's animal is also killed.

keyTerms.meaning: is it not that...? (starts a proof)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Another explanation,
so that an animal should not pass through the marketplace
and people will say:
"This is the one because of which so-and-so was stoned."
Is it not...?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is about to finish its point; the rest of the sentence is on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דָּבָר אַחֵר, שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא בְּהֵמָה עוֹבֶרֶת בַּשּׁוּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אביי/רבא discussion and returns to the question about an animal used in רביעה by a גוי, bringing a proof from the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Whether an animal used in רביעה by a גוי is killed
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's second reason: the animal passing in the marketplace would remind people of the stoned person
